title: Dynamic kernel budget allocator for heterogeneous prefill scheduling
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Background: With the v2->v3 rollout we observed mixed outcomes across tenants: some saw throughput gains, others saw 99th-percentile decode regressions driven by kernel oscillation and memory pressure during large prefill windows. Rather than a static kernel preference per model, we propose a dynamic kernel budget allocator that adjusts allowed kernel usage per-tenant and per-request-phase (prefill vs decode) based on run-time signals. Goals: reduce tail latency regressions while preserving v3's median throughput wins, support multi-tenant isolation, and make rollouts safer by limiting oscillation across heterogeneous workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-tenant kernel budget metric and enforcement hook
Allocator adapts budgets using memory-urgency and latency-slo signals within 1s windows
End-to-end tests show <=5% customer-facing tail latency regression compared to baseline for tenants previously regressed
Median token throughput for v3-enabled tenants improves or remains neutral compared to prior behavior
Playbook written for escalating when allocator hits hard limits and for manually pinning tenants to v2/v3
tasks: Design allocator state machine and scoring (memory_urgency, kv_cache_pressure, decode_99, startup_jitter)
Implement control-plane APIs for per-tenant budgets and real-time overrides
Wire allocator into kernel selector with phase-aware (prefill/decode) enforcement
Add telemetry: kernel_churn_rate, budget_throttles, per-tenant decode_p99
Run canary across 5 tenants with diverse workload shapes and collect 72h traces
Integrate automatic fallback policy: throttle v3 when memory_urgency>0.7 and route to v2 for new long-prefill requests
decisions: Use a lightweight exponential moving average (EMA) for short-window signals instead of per-request heavy profiling to keep overhead <1%
Score components: memory_urgency (0-1), decode_p99_delta (relative), recent_kernel_churn — combined via weighted sum (weights tunable via feature flags)
Allocate separate budgets for prefill and decode phases; reserves for decode must be >= 20% of total to protect latency-sensitive work
notes: Memory_urgency defined as (active_workspace_bytes / safe_workspace_limit) clipped to [0,1] — computed per-GPU shard
Prefill windows with long contexts amplify KV cache pressure; allocator favors v2 for extremely long prefill shapes in current cluster configs
We will add a kprobe-style microbenchmark harness to measure kernel handoff cost (ms) between v2 and v3 on representative shapes
This approach complements the existing kernel prober: prober detects compatibility, allocator enforces stability and SLOs

implementation_notes: Control-loop frequency: default 1s, configurable per-cluster via runtime flags
Fallback: if allocator cannot make a safe decision (missing telemetry) default to conservative v2-only for new long prefill requests
Expose debugging endpoint /runtime/debug/kernel-budgets for on-call to inspect current per-tenant state
